_comment: Universal Login copy overrides, applied by:
npm run bootstrap -- --provision-auth0-branding --stage <name>
Keys beginning with _ are stripped before this is sent (withoutComments in
../auth0.ts) — the Management API rejects unknown fields.
Each entry becomes PUT /api/v2/prompts/{prompt}/custom-text/{language}. The
key inside a prompt is the SCREEN, which is why 'login' and 'signup' appear
twice: prompt 'login' owns screen 'login'.
Both prompts carry the same description on purpose. Auth0's defaults are
'Log in to {companyName} to continue to {clientName}.' and its Sign Up
counterpart, so overriding only one leaves the two screens reading
differently.
The titles deliberately do NOT match, which is the one thing Auth0's default
gets wrong by giving both screens the same 'Welcome'. Login sits behind a
'Don't have an account? Sign up' link, so it is the returning-user screen and
'Welcome back' is what it means. Naming the product belongs on signup, where
it is the visitor's first contact — on login it would be the second time
'BoxLite' appears in 50px, the first being the wordmark logo directly above.
NOT LOCALLY VERIFIABLE: Auth0 renders this text server-side, so it is baked
into the page before any CSS the preview harness can override. Like
widget.logo_height, it can only be checked by re-capturing after an apply.
Note what the default said that this does not: which application you are
signing in to. On a tenant serving more than one client — dev names itself
'BoxLite Dev' — that was doing real work.

login.title: Welcome back
login.description: Agentic cloud platform for AI Agent builder

signup.title: Welcome to BoxLite
signup.description: Agentic cloud platform for AI Agent builder
